speaker: Teacher (use announced)
question: What is set forth?
premises: athādhvano 'sya prakṛta upayogaḥ prakāśyate — now the use of this path, our present subject, is set forth: the āṇava arc's application chapter opens.
inference: The charter: application (upayoga) of the sixfold path.

speaker: Teacher (path rests in consciousness)
question: Where does the whole path rest?
premises: itthamadhvā samasto 'yaṃ yathā saṃvidi saṃsthitaḥ — this whole path as it rests in consciousness.
taddvārā śūnyadhīprāṇanāḍīcakratanuṣvatho — through that, in void, intellect, breath, channel-wheels, bodies too: consciousness as the door.
inference: Consciousness first; body-channels second, through it.

speaker: Teacher (outside too)
question: Where outside?
premises: bahiśca liṅgamūrtyagnisthaṇḍilādiṣu sarvataḥ — outside too, everywhere in liṅga, image, fire, altar and the rest.
tathā sthitaḥ samastaśca vyastaścaiṣa kramākramāt — whole and part-wise, in sequence and all-at-once: every mode of presence.
inference: The path saturates outer ritual objects in every mode.

speaker: Teacher (nondual contemplation)
question: How is oneness contemplated?
premises: āsaṃvittattvamābāhyaṃ yo 'yamadhvā vyavasthitaḥ — laid from consciousness-principle to the outer.
tatra tatrocitaṃ rūpaṃ svaṃ svātantryeṇa bhāsayet — at each level make one's own form shine, by own freedom, in fitting form (abhedabhāvanā).
inference: Abhedabhāvanā: shine as each level, freely, fittingly.

speaker: Teacher (no exclusion)
question: Why can nothing be excluded?
premises: sarvaṃ sarvatra rūpaṃ ca tasyāpi na na bhāsate — everything's form everywhere shines, even his (double negative).
nahyavaccheditāṃ kvāpi svapne 'pi viṣahāmahe — we cannot bear exclusion anywhere, even in dream: non-exclusion as first-person avowal.
inference: No cutting-off anywhere — exclusion is unbearable, even dreamed.

speaker: Teacher (behold the body)
question: What is the body seen as?
premises: evaṃ viśvādhvasaṃpūrṇaṃ kālavyāpāracitritam — filled with the universe-path, painted by time's activity.
deśakālamayaspandasadma dehaṃ vilokayet — the body as abode of space-time pulsation: behold it so.
inference: The body beheld as universe-path-filled, time-painted, pulse-housed.

speaker: Teacher (beheld, freed)
question: What happens to the so-beheld?
premises: tathā vilokyamāno 'sau viśvāntardevatāmayaḥ — so beheld, he is made of the deities within the universe.
dhyeyaḥ pūjyaśca tarpyaśca — to be meditated, worshipped, libated: the practitioner becomes the ritual object.
tadāviṣṭo vimucyate — entered then, one is freed.
inference: Beheld-as-deity-filled, he becomes worship's object — and is freed.

speaker: Teacher (oneness with the seen)
question: What practice with outer things?
premises: itthaṃ ghaṭaṃ paṭaṃ liṅgaṃ sthaṇḍilaṃ pustakaṃ jalam — pot, cloth, liṅga, altar, book, water.
yadvā kiṃcitkvacitpaśyettatra tanmayatāṃ vrajet — or whatever seen anywhere: reach identity-with-that there.
inference: Whatever seen, become it there: the tanmayatā rule.

speaker: Teacher (worship and meditation redefined)
question: What are worship and meditation now?
premises: tatrārpaṇaṃ hi vastūnāmabhedenārcanaṃ matam — offering of things is worship through non-difference.
tathā saṃpūrṇarūpatvānusaṃdhirdhyānamucyate — contemplation of full-formedness is called meditation.
inference: Arcana = non-dual offering; dhyāna = fullness-contemplation.

speaker: Teacher (firmness and mantra-vessel)
question: What do they yield?
premises: saṃpūrṇatvānusaṃdhānamakampaṃ dārḍhyamānayat — unshaking fullness-contemplation brings firmness.
tathāntarjalpayogena vimṛśañjapabhājanam — and through inner-mutter practice, reflecting, a mantra-vessel.
inference: Firmness from contemplation; mantra-fitness from inner muttering.

speaker: Teacher (fire-rite giving)
question: What is given in the fire-rite?
premises: tatrārpitānāṃ bhāvānāṃ svakabhedavilāpanam — melting of self-difference of the offered beings.
kurvaṃstadraśmisadbhāvaṃ dadyāddhomakriyāparaḥ — their ray-rich being he bestows, devoted to the fire-rite.
inference: Melt self-difference, bestow ray-being: the inner homa.

speaker: Teacher (pure vow of equality)
question: What is the pure vow?
premises: tathaivaṃkurvataḥ sarvaṃ samabhāvena paśyataḥ — for one so acting, seeing all with equal eye.
niṣkampatā vrataṃ śuddhaṃ sāmyaṃ nandiśikhoditam — unwaveringness is the pure vow: evenness taught in the Nandiśikhā.
inference: Sāmya: unwavering equal-seeing as the pure vow (Nandiśikhā).

speaker: Teacher (samādhi of old)
question: What did the old gurus call complete?
premises: tathārcanajapadhyānahomavratavidhikramāt — through worship-japa-meditation-homa-vow-rule in sequence.
paripūrṇāṃ sthitiṃ prāhuḥ samādhiṃ guravaḥ purā — the complete state the old gurus called absorption.
inference: The ordered sixfold practice completed is samādhi.

speaker: Teacher (no rule on materials)
question: What governs ritual materials?
premises: atra pūjājapādyeṣu bahirantardvayasthitau — here in worship, japa and the rest, outward or inward.
dravyaughe na vidhiḥ ko 'pi na kāpi pratiṣiddhatā — no rule at all about materials, nor any prohibition: radical freedom of means.
inference: Materials: neither enjoined nor prohibited.

speaker: Teacher (sacrifice arises)
question: What of set rites?
premises: kalpanāśuddhisaṃdhyādernopayogo 'tra kaścana — no use here for visualization, purification, twilight-rites.
uktaṃ śrītrikasūtre ca jāyate yajanaṃ prati — and the Trika Sūtra says sacrifice arises toward the rite (occasion summons it).
inference: Set rites unused; sacrifice arises from occasion (Trika Sūtra).

speaker: Teacher (consciousness decides)
question: Who decides rule and enjoyment?
premises: avidhijño vidhijñaścetyevamādi suvistaram — not-knowing-rule, knowing-rule, 'thus' and so on at length (positions listed, not judged).
yadā yathā yena yatra svā samvittiḥ prasīdati — when, as, by which, where one's own consciousness is gracious: grace as the only criterion.
inference: Consciousness's grace decides — not rule-knowledge.

speaker: Teacher (all employed)
question: What follows grace?
premises: tadā tathā tena tatra tattadbhogyaṃ vidhiśca saḥ — then, so, by that, there: each enjoyable, and that is the rule.
laukikālaukikaṃ sarvaṃ tenātra viniyojayet — all, worldly and unworldly, employ here by that (grace).
inference: Grace converts every enjoyable into rule; employ all.

speaker: Teacher (tremor reduced)
question: What of tremor in steadiness?
premises: niṣkampatve sakampastu kampaṃ nirhrāsayedbalāt — in steadiness: the trembler should forcibly diminish tremor.
yathā yenābhyupāyena kramādakramato 'pi vā — as, by whatever means, in sequence or all-at-once: kampahrāsa by any means.
inference: Tremor diminished by force, by any means, sequential or sudden.

speaker: Teacher (doubt melts, goddesses fed)
question: How does doubt end?
premises: vicikitsā galatyantastathāsau yatnavānbhavet — doubt melts within; so he should strive.
dhīkarmākṣagatā devīrniṣiddhaireva tarpayet — the goddesses in mind, rite, senses — with forbidden things indeed libate (Kaula substance).
inference: Doubt melts; striving libates the sense-goddesses even with forbidden substances.

speaker: Teacher (hero-vow and doubt's nature)
question: What vow, and what is doubt?
premises: vīravrataṃ cābhinandediti bhargaśikhāvacaḥ — and the hero-vow salute — thus the Bhargaśikhā word.
tathāhi śaṅkā mālinyaṃ glāniḥ saṃkoca ityadaḥ — for doubt is impurity, weariness, contraction: doubt diagnosed threefold.
inference: Hero-vow saluted; doubt = impurity-weariness-contraction.

speaker: Teacher (prison and purity)
question: What binds, and what is pure?
premises: saṃsārakārāgārāntaḥ sthūlasthūṇāghaṭāyate — inside the world-prison it forges gross-post shackles.
mantrā varṇasvabhāvā ye — mantras are letter-natured (no impurity possible).
dravyaṃ yatpāñcabhautikam — substance is five-elemented (no impurity possible).
inference: Doubt shackles; mantra and substance cannot be impure by nature.

speaker: Teacher (no mixture)
question: Where is impurity, then?
premises: yaccidātma prāṇijātaṃ — the breathing kind, consciousness-selfed.
tatra kaḥ saṃkaraḥ katham — where is mixture there, how?
saṃkarābhāvataḥ keyaṃ śaṅkā tasyāmapi sphuṭam — with mixture absent, what is this doubt — even hers clearly baseless.
inference: No mixture anywhere in the conscious living: doubt has no object.

speaker: Teacher (disregard dissolves)
question: What dissolves doubt?
premises: na śaṅketa — one should not doubt (the prescription).
tathā śaṅkā vilīyetāvahelayā — thus doubt dissolves through disregard.
śrīsarvācāravīrālīniśācarakramādiṣu — in the Sarvācāra, Vīrālī, Niśācara, Krama and the rest (the stocked canon).
inference: Prescription (don't doubt) plus method (disregard) plus canon.

speaker: Teacher (scriptural spread)
question: What do the śāstras say?
premises: śāstreṣu vitataṃ caitattatra — and this is spread in the śāstras, there.
tatrocyate — there it is said.
yataḥ śaṅkayā jāyate glāniḥ — for from doubt arises weariness.
śaṅkayā vighnabhājanam — from doubt, being a vessel of obstacles.
inference: Canon confirms: doubt breeds weariness and obstruction.

speaker: Teacher (Utpaladeva's bow)
question: What did the teacher's teacher say?
premises: uvācotpaladevaśca — and said Utpaladeva.
śrīmānasmadgurorguruḥ — the venerable guru of my guru (Abhinavagupta's paramaguru line).
sarvāśaṅkāśaniṃ mārgaṃ — the all-doubt thunderbolt path.
numo māheśvaraṃ tviti — we bow to the Māheśvara — quoted: lineage bows together.
inference: Utpaladeva's thunderbolt-path; the lineage's joint bow.

speaker: Teacher (close of the āṇava arc)
question: What closes?
premises: anuttarapadāptaye — for attaining the anuttara state (the arc's telos).
tadidamāṇavaṃ darśitābhyupāyamativistarānnanu — this āṇava with means shown at great length — indeed.
vidāṃkurudhvaṃ budhāḥ — make it grow, O wise ones: propagation commanded.
inference: Close of the a05–a12 āṇava arc: grow what was shown at length.
